schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE `atom` (
  `atom_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `molecule_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  `element` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`atom_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`molecule_id`) REFERENCES `molecule` (`molecule_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `bond` (
  `bond_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `molecule_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  `bond_type` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`bond_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`molecule_id`) REFERENCES `molecule` (`molecule_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `connected` (
  `atom_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `atom_id2` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `bond_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`atom_id`,`atom_id2`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`atom_id`) REFERENCES `atom` (`atom_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (`atom_id2`) REFERENCES `atom` (`atom_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (`bond_id`) REFERENCES `bond` (`bond_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE `molecule` (
  `molecule_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `label` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`molecule_id`)
);
q1: SELECT T.molecule_id FROM (SELECT T1.molecule_id, COUNT(T2.atom_id) FROM molecule AS T1 INNER JOIN atom AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id WHERE T1.label = '-' GROUP BY T1.molecule_id HAVING COUNT(T2.atom_id) > 5) AS t
q2: SELECT T1.molecule_id, T1.label FROM molecule AS T1 INNER JOIN atom AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id WHERE T1.label = '-' GROUP BY T1.molecule_id, T1.label HAVING COUNT(T2.atom_id) > 5

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT T1.molecule_id, T1.label FROM molecule AS T1 INNER JOIN atom AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id WHERE T1.label = '-' GROUP BY T1.molecule_id, T1.label HAVING COUNT(T2.atom_id) > 5

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 selects only the molecule_id from a subquery that filters molecules based on the count of atoms, while Q2 selects both molecule_id and label from the main query. The difference arises from the GROUP BY clause in Q2, which groups by both molecule_id and label, leading to a different result set when the count of atoms is greater than 5.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least one molecule with the label '-' and more than 5 atoms, and another molecule with the same label but 5 or fewer atoms. The difference in results will be in the number of rows returned by Q1 and Q2.
